title: "API endpoints are vulnerable to SQL injection"
description: """API endpoints are vulnerable to standard SQL injection type attacks: https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/SQL_Injection . Since I only saw a closed issue from Feb. 2019 on this topic, I created this issue.    A script to reproduce is attached (given that the Explorer URL and an authenticated token are substituted for the one in the script). The script demonstrates the vulnerability for the txList endpoint used by the Transactions view:    txList/%27%3B%20drop%20table%20users%3B%20--/0/0    After executing this, queries on the user table will fail (""""relation 'users' does not exist""""). It's likely that all other endpoints with query parameters are affected as well, since no string escaping is performed in the source code. For example, I tested for peersStatus with this string    peersStatus/%27%3B%20drop%20table%20users%3B%20--    This issue can result in information disclosure, but also destruction by means of """"drop table users"""" statements (as in the provided script). Any user is able to destroy the Hyperledger Explorer installation by means of a manipulated request.    Remediation includes for example using Prepared Statements or sanitizing the string before sending them to the database server. Since the project is using node-postgres, I would recommend rewriting all queries to parameterized queries, to allow the dependency to perform proper query sanitization (see https://node-postgres.com/features/queries).    Please set this issue to confidential if needed, I found no way to do so in the """"Create Issue"""" UI."""

title: "Fabric v2.0.0 support"
description: """We'll do adding of this support with keeping the compatibility to fabric v1.4.x. When completing this JIRA, explorer will be able to support both fabric v1.4 and v2.1 ultimately.    Basically we need to do some works for handling the following specification change of fabric-sdk-node.  https://hyperledger.github.io/fabric-sdk-node/master/tutorial-migration.html    * Replace fabric-client to fabric-network and our query implementation  Because of removal of fabric-client package for fabric v2.1, administrative functions are obsoleted from sdk. So we need to do it ourselves. Basically we can do that by invoking function of each system chaincode (cscc, qscc, lscc) directly. To do this, we need to understand about not only Explorer, but also fabric and fabric-protos.  * Migrate wallet related implementation  There are some changes on Wallet class interface  * Event listeners  In fabric-sdk-node v2.1, event listener is redesigned. Explorer is using block listener to monitor new block commit    As an optional work item, it had better if we can do some code clean up around our implementation using service discovery.       """
input_text:

title: "Suggestion, and feedback, new improvements"
description: """I would like to propose some changes, including some that I have already done in my environment and have worked well. I made simple changes, but they helped me every day, especially in the environment where I work, which is Docker. Others are more complex and I think it is worth an evaluation and planning.   * config.json and explorerconfig.json     # I propose to change config.json to config.js in order to use environment variables in the settings. This makes life so much easier that you work with Docker. The same for the explorerconfig.json file ( change to explorerconfig.js). *[ Implemented ]*     * Improvements (I would like to propose several changes regarding the code itself, logic and rules. But of course, it will be hard work and a help would be very welcome!). Already implemented some improvements, others are still in the development phase and also in the planning phase.     # Reconnect() event in sync.js. Replaces calls to the shutDown event to reconnect when an 'unhandledRejection' or 'uncaughtException' occurs, this helps if the Peer is DOWN. The Explorer sync keeps trying to reconnect until it succeeds, so in this case until the Peer gets UP again. *[ Implemented ]*   # One config file per network (Nik Fruza suggestion too). *{color:#0747a6}[ Planning ]{color}*   # Do not make any more necessary +config.js+ settings, such as: Organizations, Peers and Orderers. In this case Explorer would grab everything from the network, just connect to the channel and start using discovery for this function. I've already started to implement, and it has worked, but I think we need to evaluate the best way. *{color:#ff8b00}[ In development / planning ]{color}*   # In the file: app/platform/fabric/utils/FabricUtils.js, change the validation conditions of 'privateKeyPath' and 'signedCertPath'. I added a fs.readdirSunc() because if it was a file it returned an exception on the system. *[ Implemented ]*   # Upgrade NodeJs version to 10. *[ Implemented ]*  -- I have a jira for upgrading to Node 10, when SDK for Node will be ready too."""

title: "Remove package-lock.json from version control"
description: """Currently, every commit changes ~ 3000 lines of {{package-lock.json}}. This makes viewing the commit history cumbersome as the {{package-lock.json}} file must be excluded from the diff. {{package-lock.json}} is used by {{npm}} to manage dependencies of the project. Installing dependencies with {{npm install}} will autogenerate this file differently for each user. Therefore, there is no need to track its changes in git. The solution is to remove this file from version control."""

title: "Allow websocket URL paths in client"
description: """The client websocket URL now supports \{host}    {port}    structure, but it is limited to one Explorer deployment per URL (e.g. _[https://explorer1.example.com/|https://explorer1.example.com/_] or [https://explorer2.example.com/|https://explorer2.example.com/_], but not [https://www.example.com/ws/explorer1/|https://www.example.com/ws/explorer1/_]_ and [_https://www.example.com/ws/explorer2/_|https://www.example.com/ws/explorer2/_]), because it is located at root.    When combining different Hyperledger deployments where a proxy is redirecting calls to them, it is not possible to run one Explorer per deployment. The proxy can't handle a call to a specific Explorer.    Allowing a path redirection (e.g.: /ws/explorer1/) would help to better manage different deployments.    Currently a hack could be done by managing headers for websockets in the proxy, but it should not be a permanent solution."""

title: "Improve Fabric config validation and error reporting"
description: """The function {{validateClientConfig()}} in {{app/platform/fabric/utils/FabricUtils.js}} heavily uses the technique of nested ternaries to sequentially validate each element of {{config.json}}.    Here is an excerpt:      This coding style is contentious, and the error reporting is not straightforward for someone who is a beginner to fabric and/or blockchain-explorer.    One way to refactor this code is to write a json schema for the {{config.json}} file. This will move the validation logic into the schema file, eliminating the need to error check in the code. Using a json schema validator such as {{ajv}}, the error reporting can also be vastly improved as the user receives feedback indicating the exact location and cause of the error in {{config.json}}. title: "Resolve licensing issues discovered by Fossology scan"
description: """Explorer source was scanned using Fossology to determine license for files contained in the following repositories   * http://gerrit.hyperledger.org/r/blockchain-explorer    From the Hyperledger Charter ([https://www.hyperledger.org/about/charter)] Section 13, all files that are included in Hyperledger projects should either be licensed with the Apache License, Version 2.0 for source code or Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License for documentation.  There are a few files in the Explorer source base that do not meet these requirements.  See the attached file for results.     The files listed under Attribution and No License Found need to be resolved. For the Attribution tab, these files should be replaced with code meeting the Apache 2.0 license.    For the files listed as No License Found, we should first check with the original contributors to make sure that they can contain an Apache 2.0 license (for source code) or a Creative Commons with Attribution 4.0 license (for documentation). Once this has been verified, the editable files must be annotated with the correct license text and/or the SPDX short identifiers (see  [https://spdx.org/sites/cpstandard/files/pages/files/using_spdx_license_list_short_identifiers.pdf]).  For binary files, a license.txt file should be included in the directory calling out the file types and the associated license.    Any files that are not covered by Apache 2.0 or CC by 4.0 that need to remain with the project will need to go through an exception process with the governing board."""
